result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/shell/dock/ActionBarToggle.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 by consequence and L-2 by proof quality. L-1: the Tools trigger is 0-width (invisible, unreachable) on mobile for every route whose action bar comes from the ColorPicker — because presence is gated on `colorPickerRef`, a template ref only the DESKTOP PaneSlot populates (App.vue:104 passes `:on-mount`, the mobile PaneSlot at App.vue:84-91 does not), so the whole colour-session action bar has no mobile entry point. L-2: the T-36 "true-button box-model" cure is dead CSS — `--dock-compact-control-padding` is structurally unreachable inside `.glass-dock`, the measured padding is 4px against a declared 8px 12px, the box is 32px against the 40px siblings the SFC comment claims it matches, and the guarding e2e oracle FAILS at HEAD. Both belong to one mechanism family: concepts owned one module below their rightful home.
result.negativeProof: Positive evidence for the parts that ARE sound (stated as proof, not as absence of looking): (1) the import graph is three specifiers — `vue`, `@lucide/vue`, `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` — and `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` is a genuine PUBLISHED subpath, verified against glass-ui 7.0.0's own exports map (`"./dock": {"types":"./dist/dock.d.ts","import":"./dist/dock.js"}`), not a repo-only deep path; (2) the component draws ZERO boundary-violating edges of its own — no `src/` reach, no `@src` alias, no `@mkbabb/value.js` import at all (the published-surface defect L-6 is area machinery it sits inside, not an edge it draws); (3) `verbatimModuleSyntax` is honoured — `import type { Component } from "vue"` at :3; (4) edict 6 is satisfied — the SFC declares no `@keyframes` and its transitions ride the shared `--duration-normal`/`--ease-standard` tokens, and the proposed cure MOVES the presence beat to the producer rather than deleting motion; (5) Vue 3.5 idioms are correct — reactive props destructure at :38 and the getter form `watch(() => visible, …)` at :52; (6) it is not a god module — 159 lines, one prop group, one emit.

defects.defect: The Tools trigger is dead (0-width, no affordance) on mobile for every route whose action bar is the ColorPicker's `actionBarContext` — the dock's presence predicate is gated on a template ref that only the DESKTOP pane subtree populates. The colour-session action bar (reset/copy/random/propose-name) has no mobile entry point at all.
defects.evidence: App.vue:38 `:action-bar="colorPickerRef?.actionBarContext ?? null"`. `colorPickerRef` has ONE writer: App.vue:325 inside `onDesktopLeftMount`, whose comment at App.vue:321 reads "Ref-capture callbacks for desktop pane slots". Desktop PaneSlot passes `:on-mount="onDesktopLeftMount"` (App.vue:104); the mobile PaneSlot (App.vue:84-91, under `v-if="!isDesktop"` at :77) passes NO `:on-mount`. Measured `.action-bar-toggle-slot` class+width, headless Chromium: 390x844 `/` = `(bare)` 0px, `/palettes` = `is-live` 0px, `/blob` = `is-live` 0px; the SAME routes at 1440x900 = `is-visible is-live is-settled` 125.5px. The three mobile routes that DO work (`/gradient` `/mix` `/generate` = 41.3px) are exactly the `genericActionBar` routes, sourced from usePaneRouter's router computed rather than a template ref. Corroborated in real Safari: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-mobile-light/picker.png shows the mobile dock as `Home ▾ | [Picker|About] | ⋮` with no paintbrush trigger.
defects.mechanism: Concept owned in the wrong module: the dock's presence is coupled to a FEATURE COMPONENT'S MOUNTED INSTANCE instead of to a state owner. A component's existence in one breakpoint's subtree is being used as an ownership channel, which inverts the dependency direction (shell depends on a feature instance handle).
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/ at viewport 390x844 (mobile UA), wait 5s. Evaluate `document.querySelector('.action-bar-toggle-slot').getBoundingClientRect().width` -> 0. Repeat at 1440x900 -> 125.5. Same on /#/palettes and /#/blob.
defects.proposedCure: The action-bar context is SESSION STATE, not a component handle. Publish it through an InjectionKey alongside COLOR_MODEL_KEY/CSS_COLOR_KEY/SAFE_ACCENT_KEY in demo/color-session/keys.ts, written by the colour-session owner and injected by Dock. `colorPickerRef`, `onDesktopLeftMount`'s three-way assignment and the `:action-bar` prop all die; breakpoint stops being an ownership channel. (Corollary, labelled HYPOTHESIS: the same null ref makes Dock.vue:143-144's Save/Cancel emits no-ops on mobile via App.vue:41-42 `colorPickerRef?.commitEdit()`.)

defects.defect: The T-36 "true-button box-model" cure at ActionBarToggle.vue:147-158 is DEAD CSS: the `--dock-compact-control-padding` token it writes is structurally unreachable inside `.glass-dock`. The SFC's 12-line comment asserting the cure landed is a false record, and the e2e oracle that guards it is RED at HEAD.
defects.evidence: Chrome DevTools Protocol `CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode` on `.dock-tools-btn`, every rule declaring padding: `.dock-icon-button` (layer components, 0,1,0) `padding: var(--dock-icon-padding,0)`; `.dock-icon-button--compact` (layer components, 0,1,0) `padding: var(--dock-compact-control-padding,0.25rem)`; `.glass-dock .dock-icon-button` (layer components, 0,2,0) `padding: var(--dock-icon-padding, var(--dock-control-safe-inset, 0))` <- WINS; `.dock-tools-btn[data-v-69d6f73e]` (unlayered) `--dock-compact-control-padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem`. Source: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/glass/glass-capsule.css; `--dock-control-safe-inset: calc(var(--dock-control-size)*0.1)` = 40px*0.1 = 4px. Measured: getPropertyValue('--dock-compact-control-padding') = '0.5rem 0.75rem' but getComputedStyle(btn).padding = '4px'; setting the token inline at highest priority leaves it at 4px. Box measures 104.5x32; sibling DockControls ('Save edit','Cancel edit','Back') measure 40x40 — the comment claims "the box lands at the sibling controls' 2.5rem height". PASTED RUN: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o15-dock-register.spec.ts --project=smoke -g "true-button box-model"` -> `Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) Expected: "8px 12px" Received: "4px"` at o15-dock-register.spec.ts:126. 1 failed.
defects.mechanism: A design-system VARIANT was synthesised inside a consumer (edict 4) through a producer token chosen without reading the producer's cascade. The consumer owns no register; it owns a wish. The producer had already superseded that hook for the in-dock case with the dock-scoped "folded safe-inset" (documented in DockControl.vue.d.ts).
defects.reproduction: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o15-dock-register.spec.ts --project=smoke -g "true-button box-model" --reporter=line
defects.proposedCure: The producer ALREADY ships the variant. DockControl has a `shape` discriminant; `shape="tab"` is the auto-sized text-tab control, and tab-button.css gives it `padding-inline: var(--dock-tab-padding-inline, 0.75rem); padding-block: var(--dock-tab-padding-block, 0.375rem)` = 12px/6px — exactly the Button-primitive scale T-36 asked for. `<DockControl shape="tab">` deletes the whole scoped `.dock-tools-btn` block except `gap`. Relay to glass-ui BH: either prefix `.dock-icon-button--compact` with `.glass-dock` or retire `--dock-compact-control-padding` from the published surface — a documented hook that silently does nothing inside the only container it ships for is a trap.

defects.defect: `DockControl`'s first-class `active` prop is bypassed; the component hand-rolls `.is-active` + `aria-pressed`, so `.glass-capsule` and `data-active` never land and the selected seat never composes — the active pill paints the legacy flat register while every producer-idiomatic sibling paints the glass capsule.
defects.evidence: ActionBarToggle.vue:88-93 `:class="{ 'is-active': active }"` + `:aria-pressed="active"`. DockControl.vue.d.ts documents `active?: boolean` — "Stamps aria-pressed + data-active; the icon shape composes the .glass-capsule selected seat." Implementation node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/dock.js:1152-1157: `e("dock-icon-button glass-specular-track glass-capsule-hover", {"glass-capsule": r.active}, …)` and `…r.active ? {"aria-pressed":"true","data-active":""} : {}`. Measured after clicking the trigger at 1440x900 on /#/gradient: class = `dock-icon-button glass-specular-track glass-capsule-hover dock-icon-button--compact dock-tools-btn is-active`, aria-pressed="true", data-active ABSENT, .glass-capsule ABSENT. So the control lands `:is(.is-active,.active,[aria-expanded],[aria-pressed="true"])` -> `--dock-active-bg` (flat) instead of `[data-active]` -> `--glass-capsule-fill: var(--dock-control-active-bg, var(--glass-bg-floating))`.
defects.mechanism: Producer API bypassed and re-implemented one level down; two channels for one state, one of them by accident. Unique semantic ownership violated — the pressed register belongs to the design system.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/gradient at 1440x900, click `.dock-tools-btn`, read `document.querySelector('.dock-tools-btn').className` — no `glass-capsule`, no `data-active` attribute.
defects.proposedCure: `:active="active"` and delete both bindings. Combined with the L-2 cure (`shape="tab"`), the producer's tab selected register applies: tab-button.css `&:is(.is-active,.active,[aria-current="page"],[aria-pressed="true"]) { background: var(--dock-control-active-bg); color: var(--foreground); }`.

defects.defect: The "desktop" concept has three homes and two inequivalent predicates; the app's own layout truth and this component measurably disagree, and App.vue's comment asserting they "can never disagree" is false.
defects.evidence: App.vue:310-312 glass-ui `useBreakpoint("(min-width: 1024px) and (min-aspect-ratio: 1.1)")` -> stamps `[data-layout]` (App.vue:2); Dock.vue:71 @vueuse `useMediaQuery("(min-width: 1024px)")` (no aspect clause) -> prop-drilled as `isDesktop` (Dock.vue:185); ActionBarToggle.vue:82 and :103 Tailwind `hidden lg:block` (width only). App.vue:305-309 claims "the JS mount condition and the CSS dual grid share one compound query, so they can never disagree." MEASURED: 1440x900 aspect 1.600 -> data-layout=desktop, label/arrow/separator visible; 1200x1100 aspect 1.091 -> data-layout=MOBILE, label/arrow/separator ALL STILL VISIBLE; 1024x960 aspect 1.067 -> data-layout=MOBILE, all still visible. Fourth mechanism in the same demo: demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:71 and demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ConsoleRail.vue:118 use glass-ui `useBreakpoint` with the DOCK's width-only predicate.
defects.mechanism: One named concept, no unique home: three composables (glass-ui useBreakpoint, @vueuse useMediaQuery, Tailwind's breakpoint), two different predicates. The shell's authority is bypassed by the dock's private re-derivation.
defects.reproduction: Open http://localhost:9000/ and resize to 1200x1100. `document.querySelector('.app-layout').dataset.layout` === 'mobile' while the Tools label, ArrowRight and DockSeparator all render (getBoundingClientRect().width > 0).
defects.proposedCure: `isDesktop` is app-layout state with exactly one legitimate owner — App.vue's aspect-guarded `useBreakpoint` result. Provide it as `LAYOUT_KEY` beside the other session keys and inject it in Dock/ActionBarToggle. The `isDesktop` prop dies, Dock.vue:71's useMediaQuery import dies, and the two `lg:` utilities become `v-if="layout === 'desktop'"` — one mechanism, one predicate.

defects.defect: One concept ("the dock's contextual action bar") has two types, two renderers and a `??` fallback chain; this component flattens one of them into three anonymous scalar props, so the descriptor's owner cannot enforce anything.
defects.evidence: Two independently-declared shapes: demo/color-session/keys.ts:17-27 `interface ActionBarContext` (cssColorOpaque/isEditing/canProposeName/colorModel/reset/copy/random) and demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:49-58 `interface DockActionBar` (label/icon/accentColor?/actions). Dock.vue:153-158 renders them through two parallel components (`ActionBarLayer` v-if / `GenericActionBar` v-else-if). Dock.vue:186-188 feeds this SFC `:icon="genericBar?.icon ?? Paintbrush"`, `:label="genericBar?.label ?? 'Tools'"`, `:accent="genericBar?.accentColor ?? safeAccent"`. ActionBarToggle.vue:44-46 re-declares three of DockActionBar's four fields as anonymous scalars. MEASURED: across 12 routes at 1440x900 (`/`, /palettes, /browse, /extract, /mix, /generate, /gradient, /about, /atmosphere, /blob, /admin/users, /does-not-exist) the rendered label read "Tools" on EVERY one — three props, one observable value, a defaulted chain hiding whether the source ever spoke.
defects.mechanism: Duplicate ownership of one concept in two module trees, joined by a boolean union (`hasAnyActionBar`, Dock.vue:41) that erases which source spoke. This is precisely the surface that let L-1 hide: 'the mobile source is null' is indistinguishable from 'no action bar on this route'.
defects.reproduction: grep the two interface declarations (color-session/keys.ts:17, shell/usePaneRouter.ts:49); then probe the rendered label across routes at 1440x900 — invariant "Tools" on all 12.
defects.proposedCure: Fold to ONE type. `ActionBarContext` is a payload, `DockActionBar` is the dock's descriptor; the colour session's actions ARE `DockAction[]` already (reset/copy/random/propose). Publish `DockActionBar | null` through one InjectionKey, make `GenericActionBar` the only renderer, delete `ActionBarLayer` and the v-if/v-else-if fork, and give the toggle the descriptor WHOLE (`:bar`), with presence = `bar !== null` and icon/label/accent as its fields rather than the parent's guesses.

defects.defect: The demo's TYPE view and RUNTIME view of `@mkbabb/value.js` are different copies of the library for 2 of the 7 published subpaths: `tsconfig.demo.json`'s hand-rolled `paths` has drifted from `package.json#exports`, so `@mkbabb/value.js/css` (10 demo files) typechecks against the installed registry tarball while it runs against this checkout's dist. The "demo-dogfood keystone" is a false proof of the public API.
defects.evidence: package.json exports = 7 keys `./color ./value ./css ./easing ./math ./transform ./quantize` with NO `.` root. tsconfig.demo.json paths = 8 keys including `@mkbabb/value.js` -> ./dist/index.d.ts (file does not exist; `.` is not an export), `/parsing` -> ./dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts (does not exist, not an export), `/units` -> ./dist/subpaths/units.d.ts (does not exist, not an export) — and NO entry for `/css` or `/value`. `ls dist/subpaths/` = color css easing math quantize transform value. Demo usage: 24x /color, 10x /css, 6x /math, 5x /easing, 4x /quantize. node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js is a REAL install (not a symlink). `vue-tsc --traceResolution` shows `File '/…/node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/package.json' does not exist. Found 'package.json' at '/…/node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/package.json'.` And the copies differ: `md5 -q dist/subpaths/css.d.ts node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` -> e0968b8d3b9a5ecabc7c8c1d01de9995 (12490 B) vs 4309648d15b521dc8281eab37ccc32a2 (10910 B). vite.config.ts:37-50 GENERATES its alias set from package.json#exports (all 7 -> working dist), with a comment stating the generation exists 'so the alias set can never drift'. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0 — the gate is green while the proof is false.
defects.mechanism: Two hand-kept derivations of one published surface (one generated, one hand-rolled) that have drifted. A breaking change to the /css surface in src/ is invisible to `npm run typecheck` and appears only at runtime.
defects.reproduction: node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').exports))" vs the paths block in tsconfig.demo.json; then `md5 -q dist/subpaths/css.d.ts node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts` (two different hashes, 12490 vs 10910 bytes).
defects.proposedCure: Delete the value.js `paths` block and generate the type-side mapping from package.json#exports in the same breath as the Vite aliases — one generator, two consumers. Or link the checkout (`file:`/`npm link`) so both sides resolve the same dist/. Either way, delete the three stale rows (`@mkbabb/value.js`, `/parsing`, `/units`) — they assert a public API the package does not have.

defects.defect: The boot-vs-runtime phase is re-derived locally with a double-rAF frame count, against the app's own stated named-predicate law, and the resulting private state machine has a reachable stuck state that re-opens the exact clip amputation its 30-line header exists to cure.
defects.evidence: The app owns a boot authority: OVERTURE_KEY at demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useOverture.ts:81, provided at App.vue:297, exposing b1/b2/b3/b3Complete/b4 and `dockLanded`; its module header states "each beat opens on a NAMED arming predicate, never a timer". <Dock> renders at App.vue:35, inside that provide. ActionBarToggle.vue:50-68 instead uses `requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(...))` — a frame count. Same beat re-rolled at useOverture.ts, useDockArrival.ts and demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue (4 files). STUCK STATE: :59 early-returns once slotLive is true, so `settled` is thereafter re-established ONLY by the grid-template-columns transitionend (:69-72); a presence flicker with no committed width change fires no transition and `is-settled` never returns. MEASURED, four fresh page loads: direct /#/about -> `is-visible is-live is-settled`, overflow visible; gradient -> about -> `is-visible is-live` (NO is-settled), `.action-bar-toggle-inner` computes `overflow: HIDDEN`; picker -> about -> settled/visible; browse -> about -> settled/visible. o15-dock-register.spec.ts:74-78 asserts overflow:visible only on `/` after a fresh load, so the oracle cannot see this path.
defects.mechanism: A concept the app already owns (boot phase) re-derived privately, plus a presence transition hand-rolled in a consumer of a dock that ships its own presence grammar. Wrong home -> private state -> reachable stuck state.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, wait ~4s for settle, then navigate to #/about and wait ~1.2s. `document.querySelector('.action-bar-toggle-slot').className` === 'action-bar-toggle-slot is-visible is-live' (no is-settled) and getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.action-bar-toggle-inner')).overflow === 'hidden'.
defects.proposedCure: Two removals. (a) boot-vs-runtime = `inject(OVERTURE_KEY)`'s b1/dockLanded — one authority, named predicate, PRM-correct by construction. (b) presence belongs to the producer: glass-ui ships DockCrossfade, DockLayer and useLiquidReveal/useBloomUp (@mkbabb/glass-ui/motion). With presence owned upstream, slotLive, settled, onSlotSettled, the three is-* classes and ~34 lines of scoped CSS all disappear — and the stuck state cannot exist in a machine with no state.

defects.defect: `demo/shell/dock/index.ts` is a dual path to the design system — a 2-line barrel re-exporting 3 of the 5 producer dock symbols the directory uses — and `Dock.vue` consumes both paths on adjacent lines while every other consumer, including this component, uses the direct path.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/index.ts:2 `export { GlassDock, DockLayerGroup, DockLayer } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock";`. Dock.vue:4 `import { GlassDock, DockLayerGroup, DockLayer } from "./";` immediately followed by Dock.vue:5 `import { DockControl, DockSeparator } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock";`. Direct-path consumers: ActionBarToggle.vue:5, layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:8, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:4, menus/ProfileSection.vue:6, scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:20, workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:98, ExtractWorkbench.vue:187, ImageEyedropper.vue:95, gradient/GradientVisualizer.vue:13, mix/MixResultDisplay.vue:3.
defects.mechanism: Two names for one thing (edict 2) via a wrapper that earns nothing (edict 3).
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "DockControl|DockSeparator|GlassDock|DockLayer" demo/ --include=*.vue --include=*.ts | grep import — two distinct source paths for the same producer module, both live.
defects.proposedCure: The barrel exports `Dock` only (that row is legitimately used at App.vue:167); Dock.vue:4 imports the three producer symbols from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock` like every other consumer. One path to the design system, repo-wide.

defects.defect: Per-instance ink and glyph overrides on a producer control (edict 5): two inline `color` styles on the control's children bypass the producer's own ink token, and hard-coded Tailwind glyph sizes override the dock's `--dock-icon-glyph` register.
defects.evidence: ActionBarToggle.vue:95 `<component :is="icon" class="w-6 h-6" :style="{ color: accent }" />` and :96 `<span … :style="{ color: accent }">`. The producer already resolves ink through a token: icon-button.css `color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--dock-fg-on-aurora, var(--foreground)) …)`. Measured live inline value: `style="color: oklch(0.471189 0.188448 9.83402);"`. Glyph: icon-button.css `.dock-icon-button > svg { width: var(--dock-icon-glyph, 1.25rem) }`; measured `--dock-icon-glyph` computes to `max(calc(max(calc(2.5rem*1),0px)*0.5),1rem)` = 20px and the sibling 'Save edit' glyph measures 20x20, while this component's paintbrush measures 24x24 (`w-6 h-6`) and its arrow 12x12 (`w-3 h-3`) — three glyph scales in one dock, two declared per instance.
defects.mechanism: Styling at the instance rather than at the design-system root; Tailwind utilities sit in a later cascade layer than `components`, so they silently outrank the producer's token.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/ at 1440x900 and measure: `[...document.querySelectorAll('.glass-dock .dock-icon-button')].map(e => [e.getAttribute('aria-label'), e.querySelector('svg')?.getBoundingClientRect().width])` -> 'Save edit' 20, 'Toggle action bar' 24.
defects.proposedCure: One root-level declaration on the control — `:style="{ '--dock-fg-on-aurora': accent }"` (the producer's own ink token) — and drop both w-*/h-* pairs so `--dock-icon-glyph` (or, under shape="tab", the tab's type scale) governs. If the affordance arrow genuinely needs a smaller glyph, that is a producer affordance token, not a consumer utility.

defects.defect: The published library forces a Vue design system on every consumer: `@mkbabb/glass-ui` and `@mkbabb/keyframes.js` sit in `dependencies` while `src/` imports neither.
defects.evidence: package.json dependencies: `"@mkbabb/glass-ui": "^7.0.0", "@mkbabb/keyframes.js": "^6.0.0"`. `grep -rn "@mkbabb" src/` returns exactly two matches, both doc-comment prose (src/subpaths/math.ts:2, src/subpaths/transform.ts:2) — zero imports. tsconfig.demo.json's own header states the invariant: "the library program (tsconfig.lib.json) never [sees glass-ui] (inv-K-1 — structurally glass-ui-free)". Both packages are used only by demo/ (82 demo files import glass-ui).
defects.mechanism: Runtime-dependency declaration that does not match the library's actual import graph — the published surface over-declares.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "@mkbabb" src/ (2 prose hits, 0 imports) vs the `dependencies` block in package.json.
defects.proposedCure: Move both to devDependencies. `npm i @mkbabb/value.js` should install nothing but the library.

defects.defect: The shell/feature boundary is inverted at the directory level: the application shell (App.vue, index.html, router/, composables/boot/) lives under `demo/color-picker/` — a feature name — while the actual picker scene is `demo/picker/` and the dock/pane-router is a third home, `demo/shell/`.
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/ contains App.vue, index.html, router/, composables/boot/. demo/picker/ contains ColorPicker.vue and the picker controls. demo/shell/ contains dock/, usePaneRouter.ts, useViewManager.ts. Reaching the app's boot authority from the dock (the L-7 cure) requires importing `../../color-picker/composables/boot/useOverture` — shell into a feature-named directory. Dock.vue already draws the same class of edge for state: Dock.vue:18 `../../palettes/usePalettePorts`, :19/:22/:23 `../../color-session/*`.
defects.mechanism: Directory naming does not match ownership; the shell is split across three trees and one of them is named after a feature that lives elsewhere.
defects.reproduction: NONE — this is a structural observation with no user-visible symptom. Recorded because the greenfield lattice cannot be stated without it.
defects.proposedCure: Rename to reflect ownership: `demo/app/` (App.vue, router, boot) + `demo/session/` (the honest rename of demo/color-session/, which already holds keys.ts with four InjectionKeys of exactly the needed shape) + `demo/shell/` (dock, pane router) + `demo/scenes|workbenches/` (features). Zero new directories in the L-1/L-4/L-5 cures then: they add two symbols to a file that already exists.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — the explicitly declared tier for this seat; not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — hover ink and selected ink are the same colour. Measured in one frame on /#/: hovered `Copy color` strokes oklab(0.454082 0.129423 0.0747343) ≡ oklch(0.4541 0.1495 30.0°); unhovered, SELECTED `Palettes` strokes oklch(0.454991 0.15 30). Identical to three decimals, because ActionButton.vue:30 writes `--hover-color: cssColorOpaque` and ActionToolbar.vue:46 writes the selected state as `{stroke: cssColorOpaque}` — one colour on two orthogonal state axes. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 requires focus/selection to stay distinct; here hover and selection are equal, and the selected state's only other channel (strokeWidth:'2') is a measured no-op since lucide already ships stroke-width 2 (all five seats measured sw:"2px").
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded for honesty: the component does get several things right — correct `<button type="button">` host with aria-label and working keyboard activation verified by real Tab landing with matches(':focus-visible')===true; aria-hidden on the icon; verbatimModuleSyntax satisfied; forced-colors focus is not actually lost because Chromium's UA rescues the authored outline:none; the 0.4s keyframe literals are pre-booked in demo/DESIGN.md:266 as a deliberate bespoke keep; and REPORT.md records 0 pageErrors / 0 horizontalOverflow / 0 darkClassMissing / 0 mainCountNotOne across all 60 captures.)

defects.defect: Hover state and selected state render the same ink — the two states are visually indistinguishable.
defects.evidence: Measured in one frame, picker route, action bar open: [{"l":"Copy color","st":"open","tf":"matrix(1.19924,0,0,1.19924,0,0)","sk":"oklab(0.454082 0.129423 0.0747343)"},{"l":"Palettes","st":"closed","tf":"none","sk":"oklch(0.454991 0.15 30)"}]. Converting the first: C=√(0.129423²+0.0747343²)=0.14945, H=atan2(0.0747343,0.129423)=30.0°, L=0.4541. Source: ActionButton.vue:30 (`--hover-color: cssColorOpaque`), ActionButton.vue:119 (`.action-icon:hover{stroke:var(--hover-color)}`), ActionToolbar.vue:46 (`:active-style="paletteActive ? {stroke: cssColorOpaque, strokeWidth:'2'} : {}"`).
defects.mechanism: one chromatic channel (cssColorOpaque) assigned to two orthogonal state axes; no seat-level channel exists to carry selection separately from ink
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/ → click button[aria-label="Toggle action bar"] → park pointer on the `Copy color` icon → read getComputedStyle(svg).stroke on `Copy color` and on `Palettes`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `activeStyle` prop entirely. Selection becomes glass-ui DockControl's `active` prop, documented in DockControl.vue.d.ts as stamping aria-pressed + data-active and reading --dock-control-active-bg — "the 'selected reads as glass' tier — never a saturated brand hue". Selection is then a SEAT change and hover stays an INK change: two channels, two axes.

defects.defect: The focus ring is a token-fallback accident (opaque near-black 2px square) that diverges from both the authored intent and the house register — and it re-commits a defect already adjudicated and cured in-repo (U.W-A11Y · U-F25).
defects.evidence: (1) :root tokens measured: --ring → "", --color-ring → "" (both empty). (2) ActionButton on genuine keyboard :focus-visible (real Tab, matches(':focus-visible')===true): outline:"none 1px rgb(0,95,204)", boxShadow:"… rgb(28,25,23) 0px 0px 0px 2px …", borderRadius:"4px" — opaque --foreground, not the authored ring-ring/40. (3) Adjacent producer control (.focus-ring, aria-label="Palette menu"), same page/instant: boxShadow:"color(srgb 0.665504 0.000101413 0.261748 / 0.3) 0 0 0 2px, color(srgb … / 0.15) 0 0 8px" = --focus-ring-shadow. (4) Under forcedColors:'active', ActionButton boxShadow → "none". (5) demo/styles/focus-ring.css:9-15 names this exact defect: "the `--ring`/`--color-ring` token it reached resolved EMPTY — so even an un-clobbered ring painted nothing", and line 4 sets the law "ONE token recipe reused by every keyboard-operable control … never a per-control literal". ActionButton.vue:15 is that per-control literal.
defects.mechanism: a Tailwind utility referencing a theme token that does not exist; the alpha silently evaporates and the ring degrades to currentColor, so token intent never becomes rendered relation (PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.8)
defects.reproduction: Open the action bar, press Tab until document.activeElement.classList contains 'action-button-wrapper', then read getComputedStyle(document.activeElement).boxShadow; compare against the neighbouring .focus-ring control. Repeat under page.emulateMedia({forcedColors:'active'}) to see boxShadow → "none".
defects.proposedCure: Delete `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40`. Focus belongs to DockControl's producer-owned register; if a bespoke seat must survive, compose demo/styles/focus-ring.css's dual-contrast recipe verbatim including its forced-colors `outline` arm.

defects.defect: Selected state is colour-only, exposes no aria-pressed, and its intended second channel is a measured no-op.
defects.evidence: Rest-state measurement, picker route: {"l":"Palettes","sk":"oklch(0.454991 0.15 30)","sw":"2px","ap":null} vs every sibling {"sk":"rgb(28,25,23)","sw":"2px","ap":null}. ActionToolbar.vue:46 authors strokeWidth:'2' as the second channel, but lucide icons already ship stroke-width="2" — measured delta zero. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value … are explicit."
defects.mechanism: state encoded as an inline style bag rather than a typed producer state; no ARIA channel and no non-chromatic visual channel
defects.reproduction: Open the picker action bar with a palette active; read strokeWidth and aria-pressed on the `Palettes` seat vs any sibling — 2px/null on both.
defects.proposedCure: `<DockControl :active="paletteActive">` — the producer stamps aria-pressed and a seat-level data-active fill. The untyped `activeStyle?: Record<string,string>` prop dies with it.

defects.defect: The disabled arm is unreachable, unexplained, alpha-only, and lies with the cursor.
defects.evidence: Measured with the disabled arm forced exactly as ActionToolbar.vue:44,57 does: {"disabledLabel":"Reset","dataState":"closed","tabIndexReachable":false,"iconOpacity":"0.5","iconStroke":"rgb(28,25,23)","cursor":"pointer","openPopoverCount":0} after 1200ms of pointer dwell (open-delay is 300ms). ActionButton.vue:17-18 sets BOTH aria-disabled and the native disabled attribute; ActionButton.vue:27 makes the only visual `opacity-50`; ActionButton.vue:111 sets cursor:pointer with no :disabled arm. Estimated composited contrast of the 50%-alpha icon on the measured light dock backdrop rgb(240,194,190): ≈2.97:1, below GRAPHICS_CONTRAST_FLOOR=3 (demo/color-session/ink.ts:16).
defects.mechanism: native `disabled` suppresses pointer and tab reach, so the hover Popover that holds the ONLY explanatory copy can never open on the control that needs it; state is then conveyed by alpha alone
defects.reproduction: Open the action bar; set a seat's .disabled=true and add opacity-50 to its svg (the exact ActionToolbar arm); hover it for >300ms; observe data-state stays "closed", zero popovers open, cursor still "pointer".
defects.proposedCure: aria-disabled WITHOUT the native attribute so the seat keeps pointer + tab reach and can still explain itself; carry the state through DockControl's documented "four-state contract" register rather than opacity; add the :disabled cursor arm; promote the description out of hover-only reach (see D-6).

defects.defect: A hand-rolled <button> re-implements glass-ui's DockControl — worse and smaller — with the counterexample rendered as its immediate sibling in the same row.
defects.evidence: ActionButton.vue:13-33 is a bare <button class="action-button-wrapper"> with a 9-declaration local box model at ActionButton.vue:105-116 (width/height 2rem hardcoded, no coarse-pointer arm). Its own parent ActionBarLayer.vue:129 renders <DockControl> for the toggle immediately to its right; Dock.vue:143,144,154 render <DockControl> too. Measured in that one row at 1440×900: ActionButton hit cell 32×32 with a 24×24 glyph (hit box IS the paint box); the adjacent DockControl 40×40 with producer-inset paint. DockControl.vue.d.ts states the violated contract verbatim: "the HIT CELL stays the full --dock-control-size (≥44px on coarse via the density clamp) — hit box ≠ paint box". REPORT.md corroborates: smallTapTargets = 8 on /#/ in all four matrices, on a route whose dock is still closed.
defects.mechanism: design-system bypass: the consumer re-derives seat geometry, hover face, press register and target floor that the producer primitive already owns, collapsing glyph size / operable target size / layout reservation into one number
defects.reproduction: Open the action bar; document.querySelectorAll('.action-button-wrapper') → getBoundingClientRect() = 32×32 each; document.querySelectorAll('.dock-icon-button')[0] → 40×40.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the entire <style scoped> box model and the bare <button>; the seat becomes <DockControl :active :disabled>. This single transposition dissolves D-1 through D-5 together and inherits hit-box≠paint-box, the ≥44px coarse clamp, aria-pressed, the glass hover face and the interruptible spring press for free.

defects.defect: A Popover impersonating a Tooltip: the help text is pointer-only and orphaned from AT, and the component hand-rolls the single-open coordination that glass-ui's TooltipProvider exists to do.
defects.evidence: Measured on every instance: aria-describedby=null, aria-expanded=null (only data-state="closed"|"open"). PopoverContent (ActionButton.vue:35-44) holds the ONLY copy of `description`; aria-label (line 16) duplicates only `title`. trigger="hover" (line 4) means focus never opens it → unreachable by keyboard, by touch, and on disabled seats (D-4). glass-ui ships the right primitive: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/tooltip/index.d.ts exports Tooltip, TooltipTrigger, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider. The hoverKey + activeHover + update:activeHover protocol (ActionButton.vue:59-88) is re-bound on every instance (ActionToolbar.vue:13,24,35,48,60) and duplicated in both consumers (ActionToolbar.vue:85, GenericActionBar.vue:11) — that is TooltipProvider's delayDuration/skipDelayDuration machine, hand-rolled. Magic delays :open-delay="300" / :close-delay="0" at ActionButton.vue:7-8.
defects.mechanism: wrong producer primitive chosen, then its missing coordination reinvented as prop-drilled state across two consumers — owner edicts 3 (KISS/no contrivance) and 4 (glass-ui is the design system)
defects.reproduction: Open the action bar; read aria-describedby / aria-expanded on any .action-button-wrapper → both null. Tab onto a seat (no popover opens). PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07 ("hover-only/unlabeled controls") and PR-16 ("no tooltip proliferation") remain open.
defects.proposedCure: Tooltip/TooltipTrigger/TooltipContent under one TooltipProvider hoisted to the action-bar root. Three of the component's eleven props/emits (hoverKey, activeHover, update:activeHover) delete outright, and both consumers lose their local activeHover refs.

defects.defect: The success flash is the only truth of Copy, it fires before the result is known, and reduced motion annihilates it entirely.
defects.evidence: demo/picker/ColorPicker.vue:323-326: `copy: () => { updateModel(...); void writeClipboard(formattedCurrentColor.value); }` — void on the promise, no await/catch/status. ActionButton.vue:92-99 sets isClicked=true BEFORE emit("action"), unconditioned on outcome. Under reducedMotion:'reduce', measured: {"prm":true,"animationDuration":"1e-05s","hasFlashClass":true,"afterClickAnimations":[{"n":"action-pulse-29f59cb1","dur":0.01}]} — the global guard (demo/styles/animations.css:184-193) collapses action-pulse to 0.01ms with `forwards`, landing instantly on the 100% frame (stroke:currentColor; stroke-width:2; scale(1)) = the resting state.
defects.mechanism: a transient CSS flourish is load-bearing as the sole operation result, and it is both unconditioned on the async outcome and suppressed by the accessibility guard
defects.reproduction: Emulate prefers-reduced-motion:reduce, open the action bar, click `Copy color` — zero state change anywhere in the tree. Independently: deny clipboard permission and click — identical 'success' flash. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5: "A transient flourish may celebrate success but never carries the only truth." PR-08 requires persistent status.
defects.proposedCure: The action returns a result; the seat renders a durable, announced status (glass-ui ships FeedbackMark in dist). The flash becomes decoration layered on a truth that survives without it.

defects.defect: The accent ink is contrast-certified against the wrong material rung and against the text floor instead of the graphics floor.
defects.evidence: Source chain: ActionButton consumes cssColorOpaque = SAFE_ACCENT_KEY (ActionBarLayer.vue:24,105; Dock.vue:35,157), provided at demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphereBoot.ts:87-91 as useContrastSafeColor(...).safeAccentCss, whose body (demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:302-310) certifies against surfaceLightnessNow("resting", …) at the default 4.5 TEXT floor (ink.ts:133). The house law two functions below, useContrastSafeColor.ts:338-352: "pass the D1 rung — `floating` for menu/dock chrome, `resting` for plate-seated ink" and "pass GRAPHICS_CONTRAST_FLOOR (3) for non-text ink (WCAG 1.4.11)". ActionButton paints resting-certified ink as an icon stroke on the dock CHROME tier and never injects useSafeAccentFn. Correct idiom exists in-repo at demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:124. Measured: oklch(0.454991 0.15 30) → rgb(153,41,29); dock plate color(srgb 0.931227 0.845921 0.816039 / 0.5392) light, color(srgb 0.376885 0.293161 0.253837 / 0.5776) dark; composited backdrops rgb(240,194,190) / rgb(85,62,57); accent contrast 4.90:1 light, ~1.26:1 dark.
defects.mechanism: contrast guaranteed against a surface the ink does not actually paint on, at a floor for a content type it is not — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: "Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence."
defects.reproduction: Read the provider chain above (source-confirmed). The dark contrast row is an ESTIMATE: the ambient ground under the translucent plate was sampled as [70,45,45] from the captured frames, and --accent-live may re-certify on a genuine dark scheme load in a way my class-flip did not trigger. The mechanism does not depend on the estimate.
defects.proposedCure: Inject useSafeAccentFn("floating") and call safeCss(css, GRAPHICS_CONTRAST_FLOOR) — the house's own dock-chrome idiom — instead of consuming the resting-rung SAFE_ACCENT_KEY.

defects.defect: A repeat press produces no visual feedback, and a JS 400ms timer duplicates the CSS clock without cleanup.
defects.evidence: Click at t=0, second click at t≈80ms, sampling icon.getAnimations(): [{"t":80,"names":["action-pulse-29f59cb1"],"classes":true},{"t":140,"names":[{"n":"action-pulse-29f59cb1","ct":133}],"classes":true},{"t":540,"names":[],"classes":false}]. At t=140 currentTime is 133ms — the FIRST animation still running; the class never left the element so the animation never restarted. ActionButton.vue:95-97 hardcodes 400 against the 0.4s authored three times at ActionButton.vue:122,125,126; the timer is never cleared on unmount.
defects.mechanism: boolean-flag animation trigger with no restart path, plus two independent clocks for one beat
defects.reproduction: Open the action bar; click any seat twice within 400ms; sample svg.getAnimations()[0].currentTime — it continues from the first press rather than resetting.
defects.proposedCure: Drive the beat off `animationend`, or off DockControl's producer press register, which the primitive documents as "interruptible" — precisely the property this hand-roll lacks by construction.

defects.defect: Motion is un-tokenised at every layer outside the pre-booked keyframes, and the hover scale has no reduced-motion arm.
defects.evidence: :open-delay="300" / :close-delay="0" bare numbers (ActionButton.vue:7-8). Icon transition measured at 0.2s on GenericActionBar seats — the bare-utility default, not --duration-normal (0.3s); demo/DESIGN.md books this as row R1 "DEAD until PKT-1 clears the dist :root 150ms clobber", yet it is live at 200ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion:reduce the icon still measures transitionDuration 0.1s, so `.action-icon:hover{transform:scale(1.2)}` (ActionButton.vue:118) still performs its 1.2× geometry jump — the global guard only shortens it. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6: "Reduced motion resolves directly to the final geometry and stable chromatic state."
defects.mechanism: ad-hoc literals and reliance on a blunt global `*` !important guard instead of the component declaring its own reduced-motion posture
defects.reproduction: Emulate prefers-reduced-motion:reduce; read getComputedStyle(icon).transitionDuration → "0.1s" (not removed); hover a seat and observe the instantaneous 1.2× scale jump.
defects.proposedCure: Delays and durations from the --duration-* / spring token families; a local @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) arm that removes the hover scale rather than shortening it. Per owner edict 6 the keyframes move to the seat, they are not deleted.

defects.defect: PLAUSIBLE (hypothesis) — the Reset seat's distinguishing hover rotation likely snaps instead of sweeping, because `rotate` is absent from the transition-property list.
defects.evidence: Measured on the live Reset icon: class list "… action-icon w-6 h-6 stroke-foreground transition-[transform,stroke] hover:-rotate-180 duration-normal", computed transitionProperty:"transform, stroke", transitionDuration:"0.3s", rotate:"none" at rest. Tailwind v4 compiles rotate-* to the standalone CSS `rotate` property, which is not in that transition list.
defects.mechanism: Tailwind v4's individual-transform-property model vs a hand-written transition-property allowlist that names only `transform`
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis. I could not land a clean live hover on that seat (the dock crossfade repeatedly re-took the pointer). Exact check: hover the Reset icon and sample getComputedStyle(svg).rotate at 50ms and 250ms; equal non-"none" values confirm the snap.
defects.proposedCure: Include `rotate` in the transition list, or move the affordance onto DockControl's producer hover register so the consumer stops authoring transition allowlists at all.

defects.defect: Two custom properties carrying one identical value, written as per-instance inline styles on every icon node.
defects.evidence: ActionButton.vue:30 sets both '--flash-color' and '--hover-color' to `cssColorOpaque ?? 'currentColor'`. Measured on every live seat: "--flash-color: oklch(47.118925176164% 0.188447570516 9.83402284231deg); --hover-color: oklch(47.118925176164% 0.188447570516 9.83402284231deg);" — identical values, on all five nodes, re-serialised on every colour change.
defects.mechanism: two token names for one meaning, applied per instance rather than once at the row root
defects.reproduction: Open the action bar; read svg.getAttribute('style') on any seat — both properties hold the same string.
defects.proposedCure: One `--dock-action-accent` set once on the action-bar root; both consumers inherit it. `cssColorOpaque` leaves the prop list. (Owner edict 5: style at the root component level, never per-instance overrides.)

defects.defect: Two props are dead, one has an undefined CSS class, and the other encodes the DOM-absent pattern the producer contract forbids.
defects.evidence: Verified by grep across both and only consumers and against DockAction (demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:38-47, which has no label/hidden/activeStyle/cssColorOpaque member). `label?: string` (ActionButton.vue:65) is never passed; it renders <span v-if="label" class="action-label"> (line 32) and `.action-label` has NO rule anywhere in the scoped block (lines 102-137 define only .action-button-wrapper, .action-icon:hover, .action-flash, .action-rotate and two @keyframes) — and were it used it would inject text into a 2rem×2rem flex-shrink:0 box (lines 109-112). `hidden?: boolean` (line 69) is never passed and drives v-if on the root (line 3), the exact pattern DockControl.vue.d.ts forbids: "stays PRESENT but disabled so the row geometry holds, never DOM-absent".
defects.mechanism: dead API surface carrying an undesigned state (a label that cannot fit) and a forbidden lifecycle pattern
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'ActionButton' demo/ → only ActionToolbar.vue and GenericActionBar.vue; neither passes `label` or `hidden`. Read ActionButton.vue:102-137 → no .action-label rule.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both props, the <span>, and the dead class. (Owner edicts 2 and 3.)

defects.defect: The tooltip title takes the palette-identity type role, violating the closed type matrix.
defects.evidence:
ActionButton.vue:41:

{{ title }}

. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4 closes the matrix across all eighteen compositions: --type-subheading is PALETTE IDENTITY (Fraunces); "control or label, including dropdown options" is text-small, Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold. Tooltip help copy for an icon action is a label. The comment at lines 37-40 records a prior T.W4-6 fix to this same line for a different reason — the role assignment itself was never re-examined.
defects.mechanism: a display/identity type rung applied to control-help copy, over-weighting transient chrome against the closed role matrix
defects.reproduction: Read ActionButton.vue:41 against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4's role table.
defects.proposedCure: text-small, Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold — or inherit whatever TooltipContent's producer-owned type register supplies once D-6 lands.

defects.defect: Adjacent action targets measured at 0px gutter on one route, and two control diameters coexist in one row.
defects.evidence: Measured, /#/gradient (GenericActionBar, 3 actions): sizes [32,32,32], pitch [32,32], gaps [0,0] — the three targets abut with zero separation, Reset flush against Copy. Measured, /#/ (ActionToolbar, 5 actions): sizes [32,32,32,32,32], pitch [38,38,38,38], gaps [6,6,6,6]. Adjacent DockControl in the same row: 40px — a 1.25× diameter mismatch 6px away. `justify-around` on a flex-1 collapsed to content width distributes nothing.
defects.mechanism: distribution-based spacing with no token-scaled minimum gutter, so the gap collapses to zero as the container narrows
defects.reproduction: Open the action bar on /#/gradient; map .action-button-wrapper rects → x-deltas of 32 against widths of 32 = 0px gaps.
defects.proposedCure: Container-scaled gap from glass-ui tokens rather than justify-around (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.7); the diameter mismatch resolves automatically once the seat is DockControl (D-5).

defects.defect: The glass-ui dock keep-open refcount can leak permanently if the seat unmounts while its popover is open.
defects.evidence: ActionButton.vue:81-88 calls dock?.keepOpen() / dock?.release() only from the popover's open-change handler. dockContext.d.ts:27-30 documents these as refcounted ("Reactive `keepOpenCount > 0` flag; descendants reflect via `data-held`"). There is no onUnmounted / onScopeDispose release anywhere in the file.
defects.mechanism: refcount acquired in a handler with no lifecycle-scoped release; layer swap, route change, or a GenericActionBar v-for mutation destroys the component before the close handler fires
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis, not exercised. Mechanism stated exactly.
defects.proposedCure: Release the count from onScopeDispose (or a watchEffect cleanup) so the acquisition is lifecycle-scoped rather than handler-scoped.

defects.defect: Two import conventions to one producer inside one 137-line file.
defects.evidence: ActionButton.vue:50-55 imports Popover/PopoverContent/PopoverTrigger from "../../ui/popover", whose entire content is `export { Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` — a pure passthrough barrel. Line 55 imports useOptionalDockContext directly from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dock".
defects.mechanism: a wrapper module that adds nothing but a second path to the same dependency
defects.reproduction: cat demo/ui/popover/index.ts → single re-export line; compare with ActionButton.vue:55.
defects.proposedCure: Import both from @mkbabb/glass-ui directly and retire the barrel. (Owner edicts 2 and 3.)

defects.defect: The tracked 60-capture visual audit contains zero pixels of this component — it renders only behind the `Tools` disclosure.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md covers 4 matrices × 15 routes. Reading shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png and shots/safari-desktop-dark/picker.png shows the dock in its SUMMARY layer in both schemes: `Home ⌄ | Tools → | Login | @mbabb`. result.strongestDefect: C-1: ActionButton hand-rolls the GlassDock keep-open token protocol (dock?.keepOpen()/dock?.release() at ActionButton.vue:84,86) that glass-ui 7.0.0 already ships as the first-class `keepDockOpen` Popover prop. The hand-rolled version is unbalanced in BOTH directions — it keys off the `update:open` EMIT (which the producer never raises on the prop-driven close path) and has no idempotency flag and no onScopeDispose, so it (a) leaks tokens that permanently disable the dock's auto-collapse and outside-click dismissal, and (b) fires release() for cycles in which it never acquired, stealing another surface's hold. Measured live: keepOpenCount reads 2 with every popover closed and the pointer parked off the dock; separately 1 -> 0 on a blur cycle where data-state never left "closed".
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE.

defects.defect: Hand-rolled GlassDock keep-open token is unbalanced in both directions: tokens leak (never released on unmount or on the prop-driven close path) and tokens are released without ever having been acquired. Reimplements glass-ui 7.0.0's `keepDockOpen` Popover prop, badly.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ActionButton.vue:55,57,81-88 (no onUnmounted/onScopeDispose anywhere in the 137-line file). Producer primitive: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/popover/Popover.vue.d.ts:16 `keepDockOpen?: boolean` — "Hold an ancestor GlassDock open while this surface is visible"; dockContext.d.ts documents the idiom verbatim: "Hover-driven dock popovers compose <Popover trigger=\"hover\" keep-dock-open>". Producer impl (dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js) watches the RESOLVED open computed, guards with a held flag, and calls onScopeDispose(release). `grep -rn "keep-dock-open|keepDockOpen" demo/` => no output. LEAK measured (counter read via the dock context provides table): [["A baseline",{"count":0}],["E hovered \"Reset\"",{"count":1,"states":["Reset=open",...],"popovers":["Reset"]}],["F second unmount-while-hovered",{"count":2,"states":["Reset=closed","Copy CSS=closed","Seed from palette=closed"],"popovers":[]}]] — count 2 with everything closed and the mouse parked off-dock 2.5s. OVER-RELEASE measured: [["baseline count",1],["after focus",{"count":1,"state":"closed"}],["after Enter",{"count":1,"state":"closed"}],["after blur +1.5s",{"count":0}]] — release() fired for a cycle with no keepOpen(). Consequence from dist/dock.js: the collapse timer, mouseleave, and document-pointerdown handlers each `if (keepOpenCount.value > 0) return`. Control at 1600x1000 (where Dock.vue:132 `:always-expanded="!isDesktop"` is off): count 0 => dock collapses on schedule (["C CONTROL: mouse away 7.5s",{"count":0,"dock":"collapsed"}]).
defects.mechanism: refcount protocol reimplemented in a leaf component without the producer's two guards (idempotency flag + scope-dispose release), and keyed off an event that the producer only emits for internally-initiated state changes, so the prop-driven close path never reaches release()
defects.reproduction: Park mouse at (2,2); goto http://localhost:9000/#/gradient; install the counter probe by walking el.__vueParentComponent.provides for Symbol(glass-ui:dock-context); hover a GenericActionBar ActionButton until its popover opens (count => 1); `location.hash = '#/mix'` (swaps the actions array, unmounting the hovered button); move mouse back to (2,2); wait 2.5s; read count => 2 with all data-state=closed and no popover content.
defects.proposedCure: Delete lines 55, 57 and the dock branches at 83-87 entirely; write `<Popover trigger="hover" keep-dock-open :open="isOpen" @update:open="onHoverOpenChange" …>` and reduce onHoverOpenChange to `emit("update:activeHover", v ? hoverKey : null)`. The producer then owns acquisition, idempotency, prop-driven closes and disposal. Architectural transposition: the hold protocol belongs to the design system, not a leaf button (edict 4 enforcing edict 1).

defects.defect: The click-feedback animation cannot restart on a repeat press, and the first click's unowned timer truncates the second click's animation; the timer is also never cleared on unmount.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ActionButton.vue:90-99 (`isClicked.value = true` written over `true`; bare `setTimeout(..., 400)` with no handle) gating the class at line 28. Live MutationObserver + capture-phase click log, two real mouse clicks 173ms apart: [["CLICK",686],["CLASS:action-rotate",693,"anims=[\"action-pulse-29f59cb1\",\"action-spin-29f59cb1\"]"],["CLICK",859],["CLASS:NO-ANIM-CLASS",1087,"anims=[]"]] — two clicks, ONE class mutation. getAnimations() 100ms after click#2 showed currentTime 275ms (still click#1's animation). Either useTemplateRef the icon and drive it through the Web Animations API (`anim?.cancel(); anim = el.animate(flash, 400)`), which restarts by construction and disposes with the element, or key the class off a monotonically increasing press id and hold the timeout in one owned handle cleared in onScopeDispose. defects.defect: `activeStyle`'s inline `stroke` outranks the `:hover` rule, so the Palettes button loses its hover stroke feedback exactly while a palette is active; the style-spread order also makes the API asymmetric.
defects.evidence: demo/shell/dock/ActionToolbar.vue:46 `:active-style="paletteActive ? { stroke: cssColorOpaque, strokeWidth: '2' } : {}"`; demo/shell/dock/ActionButton.vue:30 `:style="{ ...activeStyle, '--flash-color': …, '--hover-color': … }"`; :117-120 `.action-icon:hover { transform: scale(1.2); stroke: var(--hover-color); }`. CSS Cascade 4 §6.4.1 Cascade Sorting Order: a style-attribute declaration outranks every normal author rule (animation declarations do outrank the style attribute, so the flash survives — only hover dies). The spread order also places the component's own custom properties after the caller's, so a caller can clobber `stroke` but can never override --flash-color/--hover-color.
